topic: The Physics of Light: Understanding Refraction

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Broken' Pencil Mystery
lecture_lines: Why does this pencil look broken in water?
Light travels in a straight line usually.
Entering water, the light path actually bends.
animations: Fade in title: Introduction: The 'Broken' Pencil Mystery.
Show a pencil in a water glass, appearing broken.
Draw a dotted line showing the straight path of light.
Label the water-air interface as #FFD700.
Highlight the apparent break point with a #FF4500 circle.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Speed of Light and Optical Density
lecture_lines: Light speed changes based on the material.
Denser materials slow down light significantly.
Refractive index measures this speed change.
animations: Fade in title: The Speed of Light and Optical Density.
Show light ray traveling faster in air (#FFFFFF).
Show light ray slowing down in water (#00BFFF).
Compare rays side-by-side to visualize speed change.

sections.title: Core Principle: Snell's Law
lecture_lines: Snell's Law calculates light refraction angles.
Incident rays meet the normal line.
Light bends toward or away normal.
Math predicts the path very accurately.
Watch the light ray change direction.
animations: Fade in title: Core Principle: Snell's Law.
Display the formula n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2) in #FFFFFF.
Visualize the incident angle θ1 and refracted angle θ2.
Highlight the normal line in #D3D3D3.
Animate the light ray bending toward the normal.

sections.title: Nature's Adaptation: The Archerfish
lecture_lines: Archerfish spot prey above the water.
Refraction distorts the prey's real position.
Fish learn to aim below apparent image.
animations: Fade in title: Nature's Adaptation: The Archerfish.
Show an archerfish looking up at prey in air.
Visualize the path of light from prey to fish.
Show the archerfish compensating for refraction to shoot.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Light bends when changing medium density.
This refraction principle is essential everywhere.
It powers lenses and fiber-optic communication.
animations: Fade in title: Summary and Conclusion.
Summarize: Refraction causes light bending due to speed changes.
Revisit the pencil: Explain the apparent bend.
Close with the archerfish: Precision in a refractive world.
